decision.summary: The Federal Reserve raised its target federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 5.75 percent.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee voted today to raise its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 5-3/4 percent.
changes.explanation: The Fed increased its benchmark short-term interest rate by a quarter percentage point.

changes.quote: The Committee remains concerned that over time increases in demand will continue to exceed the growth in potential supply, even after taking account of the pronounced rise in productivity growth.
changes.explanation: Central bankers are worried that strong demand in the economy is outpacing supply capacity.

changes.quote: Against the background of its long-run goals of price stability and sustainable economic growth and of the information currently available, the Committee believes the risks are weighted mainly toward conditions that may generate heightened inflation pressures in the foreseeable future.
changes.explanation: The Fed explicitly warned that risks remain tilted toward higher inflation, signaling potential future rate increases.

tone_quotes.quote: The Committee remains concerned that over time increases in demand will continue to exceed the growth in potential supply, even after taking account of the pronounced rise in productivity growth.

Against the background of its long-run goals of price stability and sustainable economic growth and of the information currently available, the Committee believes the risks are weighted mainly toward conditions that may generate heightened inflation pressures in the foreseeable future.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 15.07% APR, a 25 bp increase raises monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 6.6% and moved -2 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 8.26% would fall by about $4.22 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year more in interest.
Unemployment was 4%, and employers added an average of 337k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.7% over the past year (December 1999); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.4%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 6.7% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +3 bp on the day.

whats_next: The statement indicates that inflation risks are tilted to the upside, signaling potential further rate hikes. This educational assessment suggests policymakers remain focused on curbing excess demand in upcoming meetings.
